value.rationale: Source identifiability using outbreak-size summary data on a known contact network is a natural question. Even all transmissibility-dependent mean outcomes cannot separate two nonautomorphic locations in smallest order ten, and a single variance supplies an exact remedy throughout the first nonidentifiable regime. The two distinct ten-vertex examples and complete cutoff make the finite classification mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary table fact. No claim of epidemiological relevance beyond independently retained contacts or observations above n=10.
